draft.title: Is KokoroSharp TTS Ready for Fully Offline AI Voice Chat Projects?
draft.body:
I came across a post from early 2025 where the author was nearly finished (about 90%) with a fully offline AI voice chat app. They pivoted to build KokoroSharp, a local, cross-platform TTS engine, after a new high-performance audio model called Kokoro was released. 

The question that comes to mind is whether KokoroSharp, given its development context and near-completion status, is mature enough for offline AI voice chat projects. The source doesn’t provide detailed performance metrics or stability info, so it’s unclear how well it integrates or runs in real-world offline scenarios.

Has anyone experimented with KokoroSharp in offline voice chat setups? What are the practical trade-offs or limitations you encountered, especially regarding latency, voice quality, or platform compatibility?

quality.reason: The draft accurately reflects the source, adheres to the persona, and asks specific, relevant questions about the TTS engine's practical application in offline voice chat scenarios. It correctly identifies the lack of detailed performance metrics as a limitation and prompts for community experience, aligning well with the brief's goal of discussing capabilities and potential applications.
